leading_positions.synthesis: Three members prefer ionizable lipid nanoparticles as a single-part prize. All three cite the pKa-tuned lipid design principle, rapid-mixing assembly, independent validation at scale (patisiran, COVID-19 mRNA vaccines), and the argument that delivery chemistry is the complement to the 2023 Medicine prize rather than a duplicate. They differ in citation wording (systemic delivery, nucleic-acid medicines, in vivo delivery) and all three name the same trio, Cullis, Anderson and MacLachlan, but each concedes that Hope, Madden and Langer have credible claims and that the three-person cap forces exclusions. Chabes proposed Cullis, Madden and Hope in the opening, so the trio is contested within the committee, and no supporter claims to have verified priority.

Two members prefer palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling with Buchwald and Hartwig and no third name. They share the view that it is mature, mechanistically understood, widely used and cleanly attributed, and that Kosugi's stoichiometric tin-amide work is a precursor that should at most be mentioned. They also agree the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize is the main objection, and both argue that C-N coupling needed a distinct mechanistic and ligand solution. Others (Aqvist, Chabes, Linke, Sparr) treat the same overlap as weighing against novelty of principle; Chabes and Aqvist say it is not disqualifying.

One member prefers targeted protein degradation with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, framing PROTACs and cereblon glues as one principle of induced proximity. The member himself notes that no designed PROTAC is approved, that Sakamoto, Ito, Ciulli, Gray and Kim are excluded, and that the two lineages may be seen as stitched together. Aili, who ranked B046 first in the opening, moved it behind B040 in round 1, and Aqvist, Somfai and Linke raise the same maturity and citation concerns.

One member prefers proton-coupled electron transfer with Meyer, Mayer and Hammes-Schiffer as a fundamental mechanism with stable interpretation. The proposer flags his own field proximity, the weak opening support, and that Nocera's exclusion would be contested. Zou questions whether the citation would be diffuse across theory, thermochemistry and electrocatalysis.

I prefer Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics with Parrinello and Car for its single idea and two-author attribution. No other member prefers it in round 1. It appears as an alternative for Aqvist and Zou. Reservations raised are the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes, impact that runs mostly through descendants and specialists, and, per Aqvist, Parrinello's later work complicating the citation.

areas_of_agreement: No candidate has majority support: round 1 stands at B040 three, B004 two, and B046, B066 and B021 one each, out of eight explicit preferred configurations, each with a single prize part.

B040 and B004 are the only candidates that appear as an alternative or preferred choice for a majority of members, and both are treated as scientifically mature: B040 is preferred by Aili, Aqvist and Sparr and an alternative for Linke and Somfai, and B004 is preferred by Somfai and Zou and an alternative for Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke and Sparr.
Members who prefer B040 or B004 judge the other to be worthy, and none argues that either is unworthy.

Attribution for B004 is a Buchwald and Hartwig pair with Kosugi as a precursor; every member who addresses Kosugi (Chabes, Somfai, Zou, Brzezinski) either excludes him or says his priority needs expert-report confirmation.

Several members who opened higher on phase separation (B043) or degraders (B046) now state that the evidence standard for condensates and the lack of an approved designed degrader make them premature. Sparr, Aili and Linke explicitly moved or hold this view.
Members agree the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside-modified mRNA does not by itself disqualify B040, although Aqvist, Chabes, Linke and Sparr all name the overlap as a risk.
scientific_disputes: Whether B004 is a distinct achievement or an extension of the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize: Somfai and Zou argue the C-N bond needed a different ligand and mechanistic solution; Aqvist, Chabes, Linke and Sparr give weight to the overlap.

Whether B040 is a chemistry discovery (pKa-tuned lipid, lipid phase behaviour, self-assembly) or pharmaceutical formulation and engineering; Aili, Aqvist and Sparr argue the former and each names the risk of the latter.

Whether B046 is one discovery (induced proximity, per Chabes) or two (PROTAC concept and cereblon glue mechanism, per Aili, Brzezinski, Linke and Somfai), and whether it is new chemistry or a design concept.
Whether B021 has unlocked chemistry beyond the original method, or has reach mostly through successors (Brzezinski, Zou, Somfai, Aqvist).
attribution_disputes: B040: Aili, Aqvist and Sparr propose Cullis, Anderson and MacLachlan, though Aili and Sparr say Cullis is the anchor; Chabes's opening proposal was Cullis, Madden and Hope. Zou and Somfai say Anderson's lipidoid work is a different contribution from the formulation principle, while Aqvist says the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid (MacLachlan, Cullis, then Anderson) is what changed in vivo outcomes. The groups differ on whether Hope and Madden or MacLachlan and Anderson fill the second and third slots, and Langer is excluded by every proposed trio.
B046: the proposed trio of Crews, Deshaies and Handa leaves out Sakamoto, Ito, Ciulli, Gray and Kim, and the cap makes it hard to cover both PROTACs and cereblon glues.
B066: priority among Meyer, Mayer and Nocera is unresolved, and Brzezinski would exclude Nocera.
B004: Kosugi is excluded by Somfai, Zou and Chabes as a precursor, and Brzezinski wants the expert report read before omitting him. The two-name configuration leaves one slot unused.
B021: no dispute over Car and Parrinello themselves, but Aqvist notes that Parrinello's later metadynamics and learned-potential work could complicate the citation.
maturity_disputes: B046: no designed PROTAC is approved, which Aqvist, Chabes, Linke, Somfai and Aili himself cite as making clinical consequences prospective; Chabes would rest the case on mechanism and independent reproduction of the cereblon work rather than clinical status.
B043: Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke and Sparr agree the in-cell interpretation of condensates is still disputed, and Sparr no longer ranks it above B040 or B004; no member prefers it in round 1.
B040: Aqvist, Aili and Sparr regard maturity as settled by independent validation at scale; Chabes and Somfai accept this but hold that the unresolved credit makes the case fragile now.

B021: four decades old and independently implemented, but Chabes, Somfai and Zou question whether it is as central to current practice as B004, and the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes raise a recency question for the committee.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Aili: research on nanoparticle-biomolecule hybrids and biosensing is adjacent to nanomedicine (B040) and overlaps with Sparr on self-assembly; no tie to any candidate and no recusal sought.
Aqvist: Warshel-school background and familiarity with the simulation community around Parrinello (B021); he says he would be careful in any B021 discussion; no recusal sought.

Brzezinski: his research in biological energy conversion is close to PCET (B066), which he flags as a bias risk to be checked against the reports; Zou is a Stockholm University colleague but not a candidate.
Chabes: work on dNTP pools and ribonucleotide reductase is topically close to nucleotide chemistry in B029 (a candidate he lists as an alternative); no tie and no recusal sought.
Linke (chair): physicist working close to the physics-chemistry border occupied by B021 and B043; no known tie to Car or Parrinello.
Sparr: lipid self-assembly research is close to B040, which she says could lead her to overweight it; she and Linke and Somfai are Lund colleagues but not candidates; no recusal sought.
Somfai: a synthetic chemist who uses the B004 chemistry, with no personal or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or Kosugi; no recusal sought.
Zou: connections only to electron crystallography and porous materials, none in her preferred configuration; Stockholm University colleague relationship with the secretary.
questions_for_round2: B040: which of Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer first demonstrated the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid principle for in vivo nucleic-acid delivery, and does the primary literature support Cullis, MacLachlan and Anderson, or Cullis, Madden and Hope? Can any three names be defended without excluding a contributor the committee regards as essential?

B040: can a citation be written around the lipid chemistry (ionizable lipid design and assembly) rather than vaccines or formulation, so that it reads as complementary to, and not a second prize for, the 2023 Medicine mRNA work? Sparr should say which lipid-assembly steps are decisive for endosomal escape.

B004: what did Buchwald and Hartwig discover that is distinct from the 2010 Pd C-C coupling prize, and should Kosugi's tin-amide work appear in the citation, be left out, or be settled by the expert report? Somfai is asked to separate the ligand and mechanism contribution from the C-C precedent in terms a general audience could follow.

B040 versus B004: if the choice is between a newer modality with a contested trio and a mature method with a clean pair, which risk does the committee prefer, and does any member who currently ranks one above the other change position on that basis?

B046: is the main discovery the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) or the cereblon mechanism (Handa), can one citation honestly cover both, and does Chabes consider the case ready without an approved designed degrader?

B021 and B066: what chemistry did Car-Parrinello unlock beyond the original method, and does Brzezinski's PCET case have a single attributable discovery rather than strands of a field? Should I and Brzezinski move our first choice toward B040 or B004 given that no other member supports B021 or B066?

Does the committee want a second computational prize after 2013 and 2024, and a delivery prize shortly after the 2023 Medicine mRNA prize, and how much weight should either recency consideration carry?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a three-way split with no majority: B040 has three explicit supporters, B004 two, and B046, B066 and B021 one each. The disagreement between the two leading positions is mainly about attribution for B040 and novelty relative to 2010 for B004. Their supporters concede maturity or worthiness to each other. Members who opened with B043, B046 or B029 have mostly cited readiness concerns, and no member has described a candidate as unworthy, so round 2 should concentrate on the attribution evidence and the novelty question. This summary counts only positions explicit in the eight files.
